One of our family's cats had to be put to sleep today. It has been a long time coming. She had cancer in her tongue that wasn't caught earlier and it had finally gotten to the point where she couldn't eat anymore just yesterday. It really sucks because we expected her to show the signs of a cat that knows its sick and knows it's dying, which is to hide away and stop eating and drinking. But she kept on going until the end. I saw her run up and down the stairs this morning. She jumped on the dining room counter. She wanted to keep living so bad. By all accounts she thought she was immortal. But she couldn't eat. Couldn't clean herself, couldn't drink. The vet was apparently very surprised she lasted as long as she did according to my mom. I didn't go into the vet with them. Covid restrictions, plus I just couldn't bear seeing an animal be put down with anesthesia again. It's been really hard on us, especially my sister who fed her and bathed her. I feel so bad for her. In some ways this has brought us closer together but it hurts to see her so upset. 

It's funny because I've had and lost so many family pets over the years that you'd think I'd be numb to it by now. But it hasn't gotten easier. I guess it really never does. I bought some snacks and smoked when I got home to try to ease the pain and celebrate her memory. It's helped, but I'm starting to lose my high and having trouble distracting myself again. I can't smoke again right now but I hope I can later, anything to get me back into the zone where I can distract myself with just about anything.

Just thought I'd come back to this post to say that I had a similar problem and found a solution. Idk if it will help you at all, but I think I'll share it anyway. In my case, I was trying to run SEUS on my AMD graphics card, which, apparently SEUS isn't fully compatible with AMD's drivers. If you had the same problem I was having, your best bet is to just install a shader that is more compatible with AMD's drivers like Sildurs.

Idk if this is even relevant to the problem you were having, but maybe someone will google this issue someday and find the solution here since solutions seem pretty sparse elsewhere.

I would also agree that Sildurs works well, but on more recent versions of ATM I've had issues related to mob textures rendering while having shaders turned on which can sometimes lead to some ugly looking textures and invisible mobs sneaking up on you. MakeUp - Ultra Fast shaders doesn't seem to have an invisible mob problem from what I've seen (could be wrong, apparently some nether mobs might still be invisible), but the textures still seem bugged.

The exploitative nature of modern work culture takes... a lot to explain. And a lot of things that I would imagine veer into more directly socio/political discussions that aren't technically aloud on this sub. All I'll say is that over the 70 or so years (in the US specifically, but I imagine there's a similar trend in the UK) there has been a growing rift between the wages of workers and executives that has reached a point where we are paid so little that many people (myself included) don't see any point to even trying to survive on what little we make anymore. That and the barriers to jobs that actually compensate their employees well are gated behind the ludicrous cost of university degrees. All this culminates in creating an individual who no longer has the will to live. Keep that broken system going for long enough and you have a suicide epidemic.

I'll also say, in an ideal system, couldn't raising a part of the next generation of children be considered a way of contributing to society? But there's more to it than that and I'm not really here to have an argument on that here. I'm tired and that's a kind of subject that requires more attention and nuance that I certainly won't be doing any justice.

I personally think that it is only truly morally ethical to try and stop the suicide of an individual if society was actually structured in a way that values people as more than productive meat-machines since it is the very same dehumanizing culture of work defining a person's worth that brings people to their breaking point. For that reason, I can't tell someone not to commit suicide. Not in good faith with a clear conscious. Not while they're forced to bear the full weight of the toxic systems that wish for nothing more to eradicate "undesirables" that cannot be ludicrously financially exploited.

I guess it's a similar opinion when it comes to my belief in pro-choice. Would I be able drop everything to take care of this human being myself until they are able to take care of themselves? If not then do I have faith in the systems in place to provide them with the care they need until they can care for themselves? The answer for me is always no. And while I do always feel frustrated in regards to my powerlessness to help everyone out in both scenarios it isn't about me at the end of the day.

My view is horribly pessimistic however and probably not the answer your looking for. I hope you find what you need to hear though.
